briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for September 28, 2026.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Carbon Neutrality Practices and Climate Crisis Response Efforts
sections.content: Domestically, local governments and civil society are continuing their active efforts to respond to the climate crisis. Seongnam City is hosting a Healthy City Symposium to address the climate crisis, seeking solutions for urban resilience [1, 2, 3], while Yeongcheon Saemaul Association and Inje Rotary Club have emphasized carbon neutrality practices in daily life through shopping bag sharing and environmental cleanup activities, respectively [5, 15]. Gwangju City is encouraging citizen participation by operating a new registration event for the Carbon Neutrality Point System throughout October [6, 9], and Cheongju City and Yongin Special City have urged registration of achievements in the Carbon Neutrality Point System's vehicle sector [11, 12, 13]. Furthermore, the Ansan Environmental Foundation is training carbon neutrality practice consultants, and the South Chungcheong Provincial Council is discussing the realization of 'Carbon Neutrality 2045' [7, 14]. These are examples of diverse efforts being made across the country to achieve carbon neutrality goals.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Accelerating Domestic Renewable Energy Transition and Infrastructure Development
sections.content: Accelerating the transition to renewable energy and building infrastructure are emerging as key drivers for climate change response in Korea. The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries is promoting the reform of aquaculture disaster insurance in response to climate change [4], and Korea Maritime and Ocean University has presented carbon neutrality response measures for the shipping sector to the National Assembly [8]. Notably, a pathway has opened for trading 'surplus electricity' generated from renewable energy facilities under 10kW [16], and a vision for constructing an ultra-large floating solar power plant at Soyanggang Dam is set to be announced [20]. The International Energy Agency (IEA) has projected that an integrated 'solar+wind+BESS (Battery Energy Storage System)+grid' platform will emerge as the mainstream in the renewable energy market by 2026 [17], and with Energy Storage Systems (ESS) being included in national power grid development projects, an increase in renewable energy capacity is anticipated [23]. The domestic renewable energy market is undergoing a significant transformation, transitioning from the RPS (Renewable Portfolio Standard) system to a long-term contract market [21].

sections.title: 🌍 Global Climate Action and Resilience Building
sections.content: The international community is accelerating cooperation and planning to address climate change and enhance resilience. In Africa, preparations for solar power generation and electric vehicle adoption are underway despite power shortages, with China and the UAE actively engaging in this sector [22]. CARICOM has approved the development of a new action plan on health and climate change, emphasizing the importance of regional responses [33]. UN Climate Change has announced a new ECCA strategy ahead of COP31, strengthening international efforts [32], and Burlington County is participating in new climate change resilience research [29]. These efforts to secure climate resilience are continuing at national and regional levels. These efforts are crucial steps towards achieving the international goal of limiting global warming to within 1.5°C [26].

sections.title: 🔴 Escalating Climate Crisis and Warnings
sections.content: Globally, voices warning of the severity of the climate crisis are growing louder, and its impacts are widespread. The world's water systems are under pressure due to the combined impacts of climate change and Artificial Intelligence (AI) [28], and concerns have been raised about whether species can evolve quickly enough to adapt to climate change [25]. In the UK, unprecedented summer wildfires have left their mark across vast areas [34], and in the US, an increase in bears entering human residential areas has forced wildlife managers to confront difficult decisions [36]. Furthermore, there have been reports that climate change-related legal precedents are beginning to erode the emerging rights of Pacific cultures [31], and social and psychological impacts are also intensifying, with support groups being held for those experiencing climate anxiety [27]. This situation casts a shadow over the planet that future generations will inherit, emphasizing the need for a responsible political response [30].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has covered various domestic and international efforts to address the climate crisis, alongside the escalating warning messages of climate change. We must respond to this complex crisis with sustained attention and action. This concludes today's climate briefing.
